q.intro.text: A tray holds twelve cookies. Maya eats three fourths of them. How many cookies does Maya eat? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

e.intro.text: Let's work it out, step by step. Press each step, and watch the picture first.

e.step0.text: The whole is all twelve cookies. The tape under them is the same twelve.

e.step1.text: Four equal groups. Twelve divided by four is three in each group. Each part of the tape is three too.

e.step2.text: Three fourths means three of the four groups. Three groups of three is nine cookies.

e.step3.text: Three fourths of twelve is twelve divided by four, times three. That is nine. Divide by the bottom number, then multiply by the top.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why do we divide by four, not by three?

t.intro.text: Leo has a fifteen foot ribbon. He cuts off two thirds of it. The first two steps are done for you.

t.share.text: How long is one of the three equal parts?

t.take.text: Leo cuts off two thirds: two of those parts. How long is that?

t.write.text: Which expression is what you just did?

t.more.text: What about four thirds of the ribbon? Is it more or less than the whole fifteen feet?

t.done.text: Four thirds of fifteen feet is four times five, twenty feet. That is more than the whole. A fraction of something can be more than all of it.

p.intro.text: Riley has a twenty-eight foot rope, and says three fourths of it is eighteen feet. Is Riley right?

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.c1.text: If Riley is right, one share would be six feet, because eighteen is three equal shares.

p.c2.text: Then the whole rope would be twenty-four feet, not twenty-eight, because the whole is four shares.

p.c3.text: So three fourths of twenty-eight feet is twenty-one feet. Twenty-eight divided by four is seven, and three shares are twenty-one.

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the picture backs every one. Working backward has to rebuild the whole.
